lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: tone, register, and audience

objective: Learners write the same fictional message to three different audiences (a close friend, a classmate they don't know well, and a supervisor) and name the specific wording choices that changed for each, so they can recognize register as a deliberate choice rather than a fixed personal style.
scenario: The learner takes one underlying message (asking to switch a shared task with someone) and writes three versions of it, one for a close friend, one for a classmate they don't know well, and one for a supervisor, then names what changed in each.
safetyNotes: All three recipients are fictional or generic roles for this exercise; no real person's name or actual message needs to be used.

tasks.directions: Write the message as you would genuinely text a close friend.

prompts.text: Write the friend version of the message, in your natural texting style.

tasks.directions: Write the same message for a classmate you don't know well, and again for a supervisor.

prompts.text: All three versions ask for the same underlying thing, just worded differently.

tasks.directions: Name the specific wording choices that changed across the three versions.

prompts.text: Name at least three specific wording or structural choices that changed from the friend version to the supervisor version, and explain why each change fit that audience.

tasks.directions: Reflect on register as a choice.

prompts.text: Which version was hardest to write, and what made it harder than the others?

remediation: If a learner's three versions are nearly identical with only a greeting swapped, reteach by pointing to one sentence in the friend version and asking 'what specific word or detail here wouldn't work for a supervisor, and why,' then have them revise the supervisor version using that reasoning.
extension: Have the learner write a fourth version aimed at a much younger sibling-aged reader, and explain what changes at that audience level that didn't change between the other three.
